content.text:
In this branch we are trying to set up Jenkins to build and run unit/regression tests when a PR is created. In my last claude session we attempted to plug in the runregression tool so that it runs regression tests, but in Jenkins the build failed and reported:

make[1]: *** [install] Error 1
make: *** [vlasov-install] Error 2
make: *** Waiting for unfinished jobs....
[Pipeline] }
[Pipeline] // dir
[Pipeline] }
[Pipeline] // stage
[Pipeline] archiveArtifacts
Archiving artifacts
No artifacts found that match the file pattern "build/**/*.log,gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**/*.txt,gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**/regressiondb". Configuration error?
[Pipeline] }
[Pipeline] // node
[Pipeline] }
Failed in branch manauref_lt1
[Pipeline] // parallel
[Pipeline] End of Pipeline
ERROR: script returned exit code 2

Do you know what could've broken the build?
I'll start by examining the recent commits and Jenkins configuration to understand what changed, then explore the build system for the `vlasov-install` failure.

1	// Jenkins pipeline for Gkeyll, built/run on our own persistent machines
2	// (see ci/jenkins/README.md for how the Jenkins job driving this is set up).
3	//
4	// Unlike a shared, long-lived gkylsoft/, each build clones the repo fresh
5	// and builds its own dependencies from scratch into its own workspace
6	// (mirroring .github/workflows/mac_build.yml), then actually runs the unit
7	// tests rather than just building them.
8	//
9	// Scripted (not declarative) pipeline, since we run the same steps in
10	// parallel across a set of named nodes that will grow over time and may mix
11	// operating systems (hence the per-node mkdeps/configure script choice).
12	
13	// Layers with a runregression MOAT (Mother Of All Tests) subset.
14	def REGRESSION_LAYERS = ['moments', 'vlasov', 'gyrokinetic', 'pkpm']
15	
16	def buildAndTest(String mkdepsScript, String configureScript) {
17	    stage('Environment') {
18	        sh 'printenv'
19	    }
20	    stage('Clean') {
21	        // The workspace (and its build/ and gkylsoft/ dirs) persists across
22	        // builds for a given branch/PR, so a build interrupted or racing
23	        // mid-compile can leave stale/corrupted files behind that a later
24	        // incremental step wrongly treats as up to date (e.g. missing
25	        // symbols at link time, without ever recompiling/reinstalling).
26	        // Wipe both every run so each build is truly from scratch: the
27	        // install-deps scripts already re-download/rebuild everything
28	        // unconditionally, but don't clear their install prefix first, so a
29	        // stale gkylsoft/ could otherwise mix old and new files.
30	        sh 'make clean'
31	        sh 'rm -rf "$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft"'
32	        // Side workspace used to build a same-session `main` baseline for
33	        // the regression-diff stage below (PR builds only).
34	        sh 'rm -rf "$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline"'
35	    }
36	    stage('Dependencies') {
37	        // Build gkylsoft/ from scratch inside this build's own workspace
38	        // (rather than a shared, fixed path) so that concurrent builds for
39	        // different branches/PRs on the same node never share or clobber
40	        // each other's dependency trees.
41	        sh "PREFIX=\"\$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft\" ./machines/${mkdepsScript}"
42	    }
43	    stage('Configure') {
44	        sh "PREFIX=\"\$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft\" ./machines/${configureScript}"
45	    }
46	    stage('Unit tests') {
47	        sh 'make -j3 check'
48	    }
49	    stage('Regression build') {
50	        sh 'make -j3 regression'
51	    }
52	    stage('Install') {
53	        // Needed by 'gkeyll runregression': it compiles C regression tests
54	        // on the fly using the installed share/Makefile, and 'gkeyll' itself
55	        // is the interpreter runregression runs as.
56	        sh 'make -j3 gkeyll-install'
57	    }
58	
59	    if (env.CHANGE_ID) {
60	        // Only PR builds run the regression-diff stages below: they compare
61	        // against a baseline built from the PR's target branch, which is
62	        // meaningless for a build *of* that branch itself.
63	        stage('Regression baseline (main)') {
64	            buildRegressionBaseline(mkdepsScript, configureScript, env.CHANGE_TARGET ?: 'main')
65	        }
66	        stage('Regression tests (MOAT)') {
67	            def gkeyll = "\$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll"
68	            def resultsDir = "\$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft/gkeyll-results"
69	            def baselineResultsDir = "\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline/gkylsoft/gkeyll-results"
70	            sh "\"${gkeyll}\" runregression configure --source-dir \"\$WORKSPACE\" --prefix \"\$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft\""
71	            // Move (not copy) the main-branch baseline's accepted outputs
72	            // into the PR's own results tree: _main_baseline is scratch
73	            // space nothing else reads afterward and gets wiped by the next
74	            // build's Clean stage anyway, so moving avoids briefly doubling
75	            // disk usage on what can be a large number of regression files.
76	            def moveCmd = "set -e\n"
77	            for (layer in REGRESSION_LAYERS) {
78	                for (kind in ['luareg-accepted', 'creg-accepted']) {
79	                    moveCmd += "if [ -d \"${baselineResultsDir}/${layer}/${kind}\" ]; then rm -rf \"${resultsDir}/${layer}/${kind}\"; mv \"${baselineResultsDir}/${layer}/${kind}\" \"${resultsDir}/${layer}/${kind}\"; fi\n"
80	                }
81	            }
82	            sh moveCmd
83	            sh "\"${gkeyll}\" runregression run --moat check --timeout 300 --jobs 0"
84	            sh "\"${gkeyll}\" \"\$WORKSPACE/ci/jenkins/check_regression_results.lua\" \"${resultsDir}\" \"\$WORKSPACE/ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt\""
85	        }
86	    } else {
87	        // Cheap hygiene check for `main`-branch builds: a leftover
88	        // acknowledgment entry from a just-merged PR would otherwise
89	        // silently mask a real future regression on the same test name.
90	        stage('Check for stale regression acknowledgments') {
91	            sh '''
92	                if grep -qE '^[^#[:space:]]' ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt 2>/dev/null; then
93	                    echo "WARNING: ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt still has active entries on main -- clear it out now that the PR that added them is merged (see ci/jenkins/README.md)."
94	                fi
95	            '''
96	        }
97	    }
98	}
99	
100	// Builds `baseBranch` (normally the PR's target branch) from scratch in a
101	// side workspace and runs the MOAT regression suite's 'create' step there,
102	// producing accepted baselines generated on this exact node/build -- so the
103	// PR's own MOAT 'check' run (see buildAndTest) has something to diff against
104	// without relying on a stale or cross-machine-generated baseline.
105	def buildRegressionBaseline(String mkdepsScript, String configureScript, String baseBranch) {
106	    dir('_main_baseline') {
107	        checkout([$class: 'GitSCM',
108	            branches: [[name: "*/${baseBranch}"]],
109	            userRemoteConfigs: [[url: 'https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll']],
110	        ])
111	        sh "PREFIX=\"\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline/gkylsoft\" ./machines/${mkdepsScript}"
112	        sh "PREFIX=\"\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline/gkylsoft\" ./machines/${configureScript}"
113	        sh 'make -j3 gkeyll-install'
114	        def gkeyll = "\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline/gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll"
115	        sh "\"${gkeyll}\" runregression configure --source-dir \"\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline\" --prefix \"\$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline/gkylsoft\""
116	        sh "\"${gkeyll}\" runregression run --moat create --timeout 300"
117	    }
118	}
119	
120	properties([disableConcurrentBuilds(abortPrevious: true)])
121	
122	// Jenkins node label -> config to use on that machine (machines/ has a
123	// mkdeps/configure script variant per OS/site). This map is shared across
124	// every independent Jenkins controller building this repo (see
125	// ci/jenkins/README.md) — add a node here once it's registered as a Jenkins
126	// agent under whichever controller owns it, using whichever scripts match
127	// its OS, e.g.:
128	//   'workstation-node': [mkdeps: 'mkdeps.linux.sh', configure: 'configure.linux.cpu.sh'],
129	//
130	// allowedPrAuthors (optional): restricts this node to only building PRs
131	// authored by one of the listed GitHub usernames — for personal machines
132	// that shouldn't run arbitrary contributors' PR code. Omit it (as for a
133	// shared/team node) to build PRs from anyone. Builds of `main` itself are
134	// never restricted, since there's no CHANGE_AUTHOR for those.
135	def nodes = [
136	    'manauref_lt1': [mkdeps: 'mkdeps.macos.sh', configure: 'configure.macos.sh', allowedPrAuthors: ['manauref']],
137	]
138	
139	// Every controller running this Jenkinsfile shares the `nodes` map above,
140	// but only owns a subset of those labels as actual agents. Each controller
141	// declares its own subset via a global environment variable (Manage Jenkins
142	// -> System -> Global properties -> Environment variables), set once locally
143	// and NOT committed to the repo -- see ci/jenkins/README.md. Without this, a
144	// controller would try node(label) for a label it has no agent for and hang
145	// forever waiting for an executor that will never exist.
146	def ownedLabels = (env.CI_OWNED_NODE_LABELS ?: '').split(',').collect { it.trim() }.findAll { it }
147	if (!ownedLabels) {
148	    error("CI_OWNED_NODE_LABELS is not set on this controller (Manage Jenkins -> System -> Global properties -> Environment variables). Set it to a comma-separated list of the node label(s) this controller owns, e.g. 'manauref_lt1'. See ci/jenkins/README.md.")
149	}
150	def myNodes = nodes.findAll { label, cfg -> ownedLabels.contains(label) }
151	
152	def branches = myNodes.collectEntries { label, cfg ->
153	    [(label): {
154	        if (env.CHANGE_AUTHOR && cfg.allowedPrAuthors && !cfg.allowedPrAuthors.contains(env.CHANGE_AUTHOR)) {
155	            echo "Skipping ${label}: PR author '${env.CHANGE_AUTHOR}' is not in this node's allowedPrAuthors ${cfg.allowedPrAuthors}."
156	            return
157	        }
158	        node(label) {
159	            checkout scm
160	            try {
161	                buildAndTest(cfg.mkdeps, cfg.configure)
162	            } finally {
163	                archiveArtifacts allowEmptyArchive: true, artifacts: 'build/**/*.log,gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**/*.txt,gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**/regressiondb'
164	            }
165	        }
166	    }]
167	}
168	
169	parallel(branches)
170

content.text: I've traced how the `Install` stage was newly added by the runregression commit (`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile:52-57`, `make -j3 gkeyll-install`), which recurses through `core-install → moments-install → vlasov-install → gyrokinetic-install → pkpm-install` (each just `cd X && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-X install`, e.g. `Makefile:333-334`). The `vlasov` `install` target itself (`vlasov/Makefile-vlasov:198-208`) does `mkdir_p`, then `cp` headers and `cp -f $(LLIB)` the shared lib — and that's the one that failed. But the log snippet you pasted only shows the tail (`Error 1`/`Error 2` + the archiveArtifacts warning), not the actual failing command's output, so I can't tell yet whether it's e.g. a missing `$(LLIB)` (stale/racy build), a bad header glob, a permission issue, or something else.

# Fix parallel-make race in `gkeyll-install`

## Context

The Jenkins CI on this branch recently gained a "runregression" stage
(`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`, commit `9df046286`) that added a new `Install`
stage running `make -j3 gkeyll-install`, plus a `buildRegressionBaseline()`
step that builds a fresh `main`-branch checkout from scratch and also runs
`make -j3 gkeyll-install` on it (with no prior `make check`/`make regression`
step to pre-build things). The build failed with:

```
cp: ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so: No such file or directory
make[1]: *** [install] Error 1
make: *** [vlasov-install] Error 2
```

Full log (`/Users/mfrancis/Downloads/run_10.txt`) shows the actual cause:
right before the failed `cp`, the *same* link command ran twice back-to-back:

```
23787: cc -shared -o ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so ... (macOS link recipe)
23789: cc -shared -o ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so ... (identical command again)
23795: cp -f ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so .../gkeyll/lib/libg0vlasov.so
23796: cp: ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so: No such file or directory
```

Root cause is in the top-level `Makefile`:

```makefile
gkeyll: ${BUILD_APP} ## Build Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll gkeyll

gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install gkeyll ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

`gkeyll-install` has two prerequisites, `${BUILD_APP}-install` (e.g.
`pkpm-install`, which chains `gyrokinetic-install -> vlasov-install ->
moments-install -> core-install`, each doing `install: all` in its own
Makefile) and `gkeyll` (which chains through the plain, non-install
`${BUILD_APP}` build targets, e.g. `pkpm -> gyrokinetic -> vlasov -> ...`).
Both chains ultimately build the *same* `../build/<module>/libg0<module>.so`
files. Make has no ordering edge between these two sibling prerequisites, so
under `-j3` it is free to run them concurrently — each is a separate
recursive `cd module && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-module ...` process with no
shared coordination, so both can decide `libg0vlasov.so` is stale and run
the link recipe at the same time, racing on the same output file. This is
the same class of bug fixed before for `make -j3 check` (`ac41dc7b7`,
`36db859e4`) — it just hadn't been exercised for `install` until this new
Jenkins stage started calling `make -j3 gkeyll-install` on a from-scratch
tree (the main workspace's own `Install` stage didn't hit it only because
the preceding `make -j3 check`/`make -j3 regression` stages had already
built everything, so both prerequisite chains found nothing to do and never
raced).

`gkeyll`'s Makefile (`gkeyll/Makefile-gkeyll`) already has its own local
`install: gkeyll-install cgkeyll-install gkeyll-header` target, whose local
`gkeyll-install: gkeyll.c ${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}` prerequisite builds the
gkeyll binary itself, linking against `${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}` (the
`../build/<BUILD_APP>/libg0<BUILD_APP>.so`). That file is already guaranteed
up to date by `${BUILD_APP}-install`'s `install: all` chain. So the
top-level `gkeyll` prerequisite of `gkeyll-install` is redundant — it exists
to make sure the build-dir libs are ready before linking the executable, but
`${BUILD_APP}-install` already ensures that as a side effect of its own
`all` prerequisite.

## Fix

In `Makefile`, drop the redundant `gkeyll` prerequisite from `gkeyll-install`
so there is a single, ordered dependency chain instead of two racing ones:

```makefile
gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

This removes the concurrent-build race entirely (only one chain now builds
`../build/**/libg0*.so`), while `Makefile-gkeyll`'s own `install` target
still builds the `gkeyll` binary itself via its local `gkeyll-install`
prerequisite — no functional loss, just serialized instead of duplicated.

## Verification

1. From a clean tree (`make clean && rm -rf gkylsoft`), run the mkdeps +
   configure scripts, then run `make -j8 gkeyll-install` directly (skipping
   `make check`/`make regression`, mirroring `buildRegressionBaseline` in
   the Jenkinsfile) and confirm it completes with no duplicate
   `cc -shared -o .../libg0*.so` lines for any module and no `cp: ... No
   such file or directory` errors.
2. Repeat a couple of times (the race is nondeterministic / parallelism- and
   timing-dependent) to build confidence it's actually fixed, not just
   lucky.
3. Push and let the Jenkins PR build re-run end-to-end, confirming the
   `Install`, `Regression baseline (main)`, and `Regression tests (MOAT)`
   stages all pass and `archiveArtifacts` picks up the expected
   `gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**` files.

# Fix Jenkins install race: use `install`, and fix the `gkeyll-install` race too

## Context

The Jenkins CI on this branch recently gained a "runregression" stage
(`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`, commit `9df046286`) that added an `Install` stage
running `make -j3 gkeyll-install`, plus a `buildRegressionBaseline()` step
that builds a fresh `main`-branch checkout from scratch and also runs
`make -j3 gkeyll-install` on it (with no prior `make check`/`make regression`
to pre-build things). The build failed with:

```
cp: ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so: No such file or directory
make[1]: *** [install] Error 1
make: *** [vlasov-install] Error 2
```

The fuller log (`/Users/mfrancis/Downloads/run_10.txt`) shows the actual
cause: right before the failed `cp`, the *same* link command ran twice
back-to-back:

```
23787: cc -shared -o ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so ...
23789: cc -shared -o ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so ...   (identical, again)
23795: cp -f ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so .../gkeyll/lib/libg0vlasov.so
23796: cp: ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so: No such file or directory
```

**Root cause.** In the top-level `Makefile`:

```makefile
gkeyll: ${BUILD_APP} ## Build Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll gkeyll

gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install gkeyll ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

`gkeyll-install` has two sibling prerequisites — `${BUILD_APP}-install`
(chains `pkpm-install -> gyrokinetic-install -> vlasov-install ->
moments-install -> core-install`, each doing `install: all`) and `gkeyll`
(chains through the plain `${BUILD_APP}` build targets, e.g.
`pkpm -> gyrokinetic -> vlasov -> ...`). Both chains build the *same*
`../build/<module>/libg0<module>.so` files, and Make has no ordering edge
between them, so under `-j3` it can run both concurrently — each is a
separate recursive `cd module && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-module ...` process
with no shared coordination, so both raced to relink `libg0vlasov.so` at
once. Same class of bug as the parallel-`make check` races fixed before
(`ac41dc7b7`, `36db859e4`); it just hadn't been exercised for `install`
until this new Jenkins stage ran `make -j3 gkeyll-install` on a from-scratch
tree. (The main workspace's own `Install` stage didn't hit it only because
the preceding `make -j3 check`/`make -j3 regression` had already built
everything, so both chains found nothing to do and never raced.)

**Why the user's everyday `make -j3 install` never hits this:** `install`
is a *different* target, not defined in the top-level `Makefile` at all —
it comes from `alltargets.mak`, which `configure` generates and the
Makefile `-include`s (`Makefile:29`):

```makefile
# alltargets.mak (generated automatically)
install: pkpm-install ## Install gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

This has a single prerequisite chain (`pkpm-install`, i.e. `${BUILD_APP}-install`)
— no second chain racing to rebuild the same `.so` files — and its recipe
ends up in the exact same place (`cd gkeyll && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-gkeyll
install`) as `gkeyll-install`. So it's a safe, drop-in replacement for what
Jenkins is doing.

## Fix (two parts)

**1. Jenkins: call `install` instead of `gkeyll-install`** (unblocks CI,
matches the proven-stable everyday workflow). In
`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`, change both occurrences:
- line 56 (`buildAndTest`'s `Install` stage)
- line 113 (`buildRegressionBaseline`)

from `sh 'make -j3 gkeyll-install'` to `sh 'make -j3 install'`.

**2. Makefile: fix the latent race in `gkeyll-install` anyway** (defense in
depth — it's still a real, shipped target; anyone building with `-j` could
hit the same race). Drop the redundant `gkeyll` prerequisite:

```makefile
gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

This is safe because `Makefile-gkeyll`'s own `install` target already
depends on its local `gkeyll-install` target (`gkeyll.c ${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}`),
which builds the `gkeyll` binary itself — and `${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}`
(`../build/<BUILD_APP>/libg0<BUILD_APP>.so`) is already guaranteed built by
`${BUILD_APP}-install`'s own `all` prerequisite. So no functionality is
lost, just de-duplicated/serialized instead of raced.

## Verification

1. From a clean tree (`make clean && rm -rf gkylsoft`), run mkdeps +
   configure, then run `make -j8 gkeyll-install` directly (skipping
   `check`/`regression`, mirroring `buildRegressionBaseline`) and confirm it
   completes with no duplicate `cc -shared -o .../libg0*.so` lines and no
   `cp: ... No such file or directory` errors. Repeat a couple of times
   since the race is timing-dependent.
2. Confirm `make -j8 install` (the target Jenkins will now use) still works
   as it always has for the user's normal workflow — no behavior change
   expected there, just a sanity check.
3. Push and let the Jenkins PR build re-run end-to-end, confirming
   `Install`, `Regression baseline (main)`, and `Regression tests (MOAT)`
   all pass and `archiveArtifacts` picks up the expected
   `gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**` files.

## Part 3: fix the `buildRegressionBaseline` checkout timeout

### Context

After Parts 1-2 above were pushed, Jenkins re-ran the PR (`run_11.txt`).
The `Install` stage now passes cleanly (confirming the race fix worked),
but the very next stage, `Regression baseline (main)`, failed:

```
[Pipeline] { (Regression baseline (main))
[Pipeline] dir
[Pipeline] { checkout
Cloning repository https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll
 > git init .../_main_baseline/gkylsoft  # fresh, empty git dir
 > git fetch --tags --force --progress -- https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
remote: Enumerating objects: 138298, done.
ERROR: Timeout after 10 minutes
ERROR: Error cloning remote repo 'origin'
```

This is unrelated to the install race — it's a plain slow/oversized git
checkout. `buildRegressionBaseline` (`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile:112-117`)
checks out the baseline branch with a bare `GitSCM` step that has no
refspec or clone options configured:

```groovy

23795: cp -f ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so .../gkeyll/lib/libg0vlasov.so
23796: cp: ../build/vlasov/libg0vlasov.so: No such file or directory
```

**Root cause.** In the top-level `Makefile`:

```makefile
gkeyll: ${BUILD_APP} ## Build Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll gkeyll

gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install gkeyll ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

`gkeyll-install` has two sibling prerequisites — `${BUILD_APP}-install`
(chains `pkpm-install -> gyrokinetic-install -> vlasov-install ->
moments-install -> core-install`, each doing `install: all`) and `gkeyll`
(chains through the plain `${BUILD_APP}` build targets, e.g.
`pkpm -> gyrokinetic -> vlasov -> ...`). Both chains build the *same*
`../build/<module>/libg0<module>.so` files, and Make has no ordering edge
between them, so under `-j3` it can run both concurrently — each is a
separate recursive `cd module && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-module ...` process
with no shared coordination, so both raced to relink `libg0vlasov.so` at
once. Same class of bug as the parallel-`make check` races fixed before
(`ac41dc7b7`, `36db859e4`); it just hadn't been exercised for `install`
until this new Jenkins stage ran `make -j3 gkeyll-install` on a from-scratch
tree. (The main workspace's own `Install` stage didn't hit it only because
the preceding `make -j3 check`/`make -j3 regression` had already built
everything, so both chains found nothing to do and never raced.)

**Why the user's everyday `make -j3 install` never hits this:** `install`
is a *different* target, not defined in the top-level `Makefile` at all —
it comes from `alltargets.mak`, which `configure` generates and the
Makefile `-include`s (`Makefile:29`):

```makefile
# alltargets.mak (generated automatically)
install: pkpm-install ## Install gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

This has a single prerequisite chain (`pkpm-install`, i.e. `${BUILD_APP}-install`)
— no second chain racing to rebuild the same `.so` files — and its recipe
ends up in the exact same place (`cd gkeyll && $(MAKE) -f Makefile-gkeyll
install`) as `gkeyll-install`. So it's a safe, drop-in replacement for what
Jenkins is doing.

## Fix (two parts)

**1. Jenkins: call `install` instead of `gkeyll-install`** (unblocks CI,
matches the proven-stable everyday workflow). In
`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`, change both occurrences:
- line 56 (`buildAndTest`'s `Install` stage)
- line 113 (`buildRegressionBaseline`)

from `sh 'make -j3 gkeyll-install'` to `sh 'make -j3 install'`.

**2. Makefile: fix the latent race in `gkeyll-install` anyway** (defense in
depth — it's still a real, shipped target; anyone building with `-j` could
hit the same race). Drop the redundant `gkeyll` prerequisite:

```makefile
gkeyll-install: ${BUILD_APP}-install ## Install Gkeyll executable
	cd gkeyll && ${MAKE} -f Makefile-gkeyll install
```

This is safe because `Makefile-gkeyll`'s own `install` target already
depends on its local `gkeyll-install` target (`gkeyll.c ${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}`),
which builds the `gkeyll` binary itself — and `${FIN_APP_LIB_NAME}`
(`../build/<BUILD_APP>/libg0<BUILD_APP>.so`) is already guaranteed built by
`${BUILD_APP}-install`'s own `all` prerequisite. So no functionality is
lost, just de-duplicated/serialized instead of raced.

## Verification

1. From a clean tree (`make clean && rm -rf gkylsoft`), run mkdeps +
   configure, then run `make -j8 gkeyll-install` directly (skipping
   `check`/`regression`, mirroring `buildRegressionBaseline`) and confirm it
   completes with no duplicate `cc -shared -o .../libg0*.so` lines and no
   `cp: ... No such file or directory` errors. Repeat a couple of times
   since the race is timing-dependent.
2. Confirm `make -j8 install` (the target Jenkins will now use) still works
   as it always has for the user's normal workflow — no behavior change
   expected there, just a sanity check.
3. Push and let the Jenkins PR build re-run end-to-end, confirming
   `Install`, `Regression baseline (main)`, and `Regression tests (MOAT)`
   all pass and `archiveArtifacts` picks up the expected
   `gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**` files.

---

## Part 3: fix the `buildRegressionBaseline` checkout timeout

### Context

After Parts 1-2 above were pushed, Jenkins re-ran the PR (`run_11.txt`).
The `Install` stage now passes cleanly (confirming the race fix worked),
but the very next stage, `Regression baseline (main)`, failed:

```
[Pipeline] { (Regression baseline (main))
[Pipeline] dir
[Pipeline] { checkout
Cloning repository https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll
 > git init .../_main_baseline/gkylsoft  # fresh, empty git dir
 > git fetch --tags --force --progress -- https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
remote: Enumerating objects: 138298, done.
ERROR: Timeout after 10 minutes
ERROR: Error cloning remote repo 'origin'
```

This is unrelated to the install race — it's a plain slow/oversized git
checkout. `buildRegressionBaseline` (`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile:112-117`)
checks out the baseline branch with a bare `GitSCM` step that has no
refspec or clone options configured:

```groovy
checkout([$class: 'GitSCM',
    branches: [[name: "*/${baseBranch}"]],
    userRemoteConfigs: [[url: 'https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll']],
])
```

With no refspec, GitSCM defaults to fetching **every** branch and tag in
the whole repo (`+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`) into a brand new,
empty `_main_baseline/` git dir (no local objects to fetch incrementally
against, unlike the main workspace checkout, which only ever fetches the
single PR ref `+refs/pull/1104/head:...` into a workspace that already has
history from prior builds). 138298 objects took over 10 minutes and Jenkins
killed it. We only actually need the tip of one branch (`baseBranch`) to
build the baseline — not the whole repo's history/branches.

### Fix

Replace the `GitSCM` checkout step with a plain shallow `git clone` of just
`baseBranch`, run via `sh` inside the same `dir('_main_baseline') { ... }`
block (which is already empty at this point, thanks to the `Clean` stage's
`rm -rf "$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline"`). This is simpler and easier to verify
than GitSCM's `refspec`/`CloneOption` extension DSL (whose field names and
behavior are git-plugin-version-dependent), and this repo/URL needs no
Jenkins-managed credentials here (the log shows "No credentials
specified" for this same clone today):

```groovy
sh "git clone --depth 1 --branch ${baseBranch} https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll ."
```

replacing the current:

```groovy
checkout([$class: 'GitSCM',
    branches: [[name: "*/${baseBranch}"]],
    userRemoteConfigs: [[url: 'https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll']],
])
```

This clones just the tip of one branch, regardless of how large the overall
repo/history is, avoiding the 138298-object all-branches fetch entirely.

File to change: `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile:114-117`.

### Verification

1. Diff-review the change; the rest of `buildRegressionBaseline` doesn't
   need to change (it already works purely off `${baseBranch}` and the
   checked-out working tree, not any specific clone depth/refs).
2. Push and let the Jenkins PR build re-run, confirming the
   `Regression baseline (main)` stage's checkout completes quickly (well
   under the old 10-minute default) and the pipeline proceeds into
   `Regression tests (MOAT)`.
3. If it still times out (e.g. GitHub-side slowness unrelated to clone
   size), the next lever is adding an explicit `timeout` wrapper around the
   `sh 'git clone ...'` step rather than reverting the shallow narrowing.
